web_evidence.title: An Exclusive First Look Inside Emma Cline's 'The Girls'
web_evidence.note: An authorized, sustained interior excerpt supplied by Random House presents Evie's experiences and retrospective knowledge continuously through I, me, and my.

web_evidence.title: “We All Want to Be Seen”: The Male Gaze, the Female Gaze and the Act of Looking as Metaphor in Emma Cline’s The Girls
web_evidence.note: This scholarly article identifies middle-aged Evie as the novel's protagonist-cum-narrator reflecting on her own life and analyzes first-person passages from across the novel.

web_evidence.title: “The Girls,” by Emma Cline
web_evidence.note: James Wood explicitly attributes the novel's immediacy to its first-person narration and discusses Evie's retrospective account across the 1969 story and contemporary frame.

web_evidence.title: Emma Cline
web_evidence.note: The author interview describes middle-aged Evie recounting her adolescence; Cline discusses the older narrator and confirms that the bulk of the novel is Evie's recollection and self-analysis.

web_evidence.title: Cult Favorite: PW Talks with Emma Cline
web_evidence.note: Cline explains that the novel juxtaposes Evie's youth and middle age and that she wanted an adult voice able to comment on and contextualize Evie's own formative experiences.

person_note: The Goodreads quotations repeatedly expose Evie as a participating retrospective narrator through I, me, my, and inclusive we. Generalized you in q00983 and q00989 expresses reflections on girlhood and desire rather than sustained second-person narration. Passages centered on Suzanne or the ranch, especially q00993 and q01000, are Evie's descriptions of other characters and therefore do not establish third-person narration. Authorized interior prose independently sustains Evie's first-person voice, while scholarly analysis and several credible reviews and author interviews describe the whole novel as Evie's narration across adolescent and middle-aged timeframes. The temporal shifts do not change grammatical person, and no credible evidence indicates alternating-person sections; remaining uncertainty is negligible.
